vehicle:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original RTS unit redesign art approval board, NOT a game screenshot or finished 3D model.
Reference image: supplied actual main battle tank model preview is a STYLE / MATERIAL / DETAIL BENCHMARK ONLY. Ignore its UI. The user accepts that tank, but rejected the other units as coarse generic boxes. We must bring four other vehicles to AT LEAST this tank's structural detail, and give radically different silhouettes at long distance.
Create a polished landscape 2-by-2 concept sheet of FOUR DISTINCT near-future modern military support/combat vehicles, one large three-quarter isometric view per cell, front toward lower left, 30-degree camera elevation. Very crisp high-resolution semi-realistic pre-rendered RTS art, carefully modeled curved/beveled geometry, organized layered armor, articulated mechanical assemblies, wheel tread, recessed vents, layered hatches, sensible welds and joints, restrained wear, consistent soft upper-left lighting and ambient occlusion. NOT voxel, LEGO, block primitives, mobile-game toy or gritty photo. All four must be fully visible with generous gutters, charcoal blue-grey studio background. No environment or UI. Include tiny flat off-white silhouette under each hero as a thumbnail readability check, and a small rear-three-quarter study of the SAME design. Typography minimal, use ONLY role labels: "IFV", "ARTILLERY", "ENGINEERING", "ORE HARVESTER". This is a concept sheet; small silhouettes are schematic, not measured in-game sizes.
IFV upper left: predatory low boat-shaped armored wedge, eight large independent wheels under sculpted scalloped fenders, low compact OFFSET autocannon mount (not a tank turret and not long tank barrel), raised armored rear troop compartment, angled rear ramp, recessed headlights, spaced armor cheeks, visible suspension. Broad continuous sloping team-color side cheek panels. Distinct low fast pointed triangular silhouette; no slab-shaped rectangular bus.
ARTILLERY upper right: long narrow tracked hull, compact armored driver's cab at front, a tall EXPOSED rear gun cradle with unmistakable very long elevated single barrel, large recoil cylinders, articulated breech, travel locking yoke and folded rear spades. No enclosed tank turret, no armored rectangular shed. The big open negative space between cradle and chassis must identify it in silhouette. Team color on sloped cab and rear side protective plates.
ENGINEERING lower left: wide squat FOUR separate short tracked pods, central equipment deck, large folded A-frame / portal lifting gantry arching ABOVE the deck, visible cable winch, compact asymmetric operator cabin, stowed articulated outriggers and modular construction containers. Rounded mechanical joints, detailed hydraulic hoses. Broad and crab-like industrial platform, not a six-wheel truck, not a weapon. Large team color on track guards and equipment modules; neutral muted yellow on lifting hardware.
ORE HARVESTER lower right: rugged low articulated mining vehicle with a narrow waist, four huge balloon tires, distinctly OFFSET small armored glass cab, broad tapered scoop-like ore receiving nose, massive curved ribbed rear hopper with a visible partial ore load and hydraulic tipping cylinders. The stepped profile and waist make it unmistakably different from both IFV and engineering platform. No crane. Team color hopper side shells and cab armor; graphite tires, neutral mineral payload.
All vehicles share desaturated warm grey armor and bold medium blue designated RECOLORABLE panel zones covering roughly 35-45% of visible upper/side armor. Blue panels have proper shading and surface definition; wheels, tracks, bare metal, windows, yellow tools remain neutral. Future faction hue must be replaceable without losing construction detail. Do not introduce faction logos. Mechanical plausibility and readable dominant forms more important than scattered rivets. Match or exceed accepted tank quality, not its silhouette.
infantry:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original modern RTS infantry redesign approval board. Reference 1: accepted actual tank screenshot, use ONLY as minimum structural quality and palette/material cohesion benchmark, ignore UI. Reference 2: earlier infantry concept sheet, useful fidelity benchmark but its three bodies are too similar; DO NOT repeat identical torso/leg/backpack silhouettes.
Design three polished, sophisticated near-future modern infantry roles recognizable by body shape from far away, not just weapon changes. One landscape triptych with large front-three-quarter 30deg elevated full body view for each role, one smaller corresponding rear-three-quarter view, and a tiny flat silhouette below. Plain charcoal blue-grey background with clean gutters. Text only: "RIFLEMAN", "ANTI-ARMOR", "ENGINEER".
Natural articulated human anatomy, excellent cloth folds, gloves, boots with soles, shoulder plate thickness, harness straps and buckles, layered equipment, well-formed faces, material differences. High-quality semi-realistic stylized pre-rendered RTS aesthetic, smooth forms and crisp edges, NOT LEGO, mannequin, chunky low-poly, cheap block model or hyperreal gritty film concept. Clear simple dominant shapes first, secondary equipment detail second. Not fantasy and no giant robot.
RIFLEMAN: lean athletic forward combat stance, compact close-fitting helmet with low goggles, angled lightweight chest armor, short split tactical overshirt at hips, compact single sling pack, a short rifle carried ready at waist. Narrow agile silhouette and low profile. One modest raised angular shoulder pad; unobstructed arms and legs.
ANTI-ARMOR: a heavier real human with thick high collar, broad protective shoulder yoke, layered thigh and knee armor, weight distributed in wide planted stance, one large long shoulder-mounted anti-armor launcher creating dominant diagonal top silhouette, rear upright reload tube integrated with a compact support frame. Broad upper body but anatomically believable, no powered armor fantasy; visible recoil pad, straps, tube caps, optics. A silhouette distinct from a rifleman holding a different gun.
ENGINEER: practical mechanic soldier with short yellow hardhat and raised protective face visor, mid-weight utility jacket with rolled-up sleeves, pronounced asymmetric hip toolbox, a compact tall rectangular equipment backpack with top carry handle and spooled cable, knee pads, one hand carrying a hefty folded power tool. One short folded manipulator arm attached to backpack, not a weapon, believable construction machinery. Distinct tall-back / offset-wide-hip outline. Avoid oversized cartoon wrench. No gun.
Consistent subdued warm-grey cloth, olive neutral armor and graphite equipment. Broad medium blue recolorable surfaces on chest, upper sleeves/shoulders and backpacks, roughly 35-45% of upper-body projected area. Preserve folds and shading on blue. Metal, skin, yellow helmet, boots, weapons and tools remain neutral. Faction recoloring must be able to replace blue later, not red-blue duplicated people. Small studies must show same physical equipment and costume as their respective main view. Ground-contact soft shadow, consistent upper-left studio light, keep all feet and equipment within frame. No environment, no game UI, no logos, no futuristic glowing lights. Small silhouettes are conceptual readability studies not actual runtime screenshots. Prioritize a refined coherent design that can subsequently be modeled faithfully; not a generic soldier pack.
